name_reason: Conforms to fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>. '22' is the dispatch-table index 0x22 (data at 0x51C19; a domain ID, not an address residue). Descriptor corrected from '__unref_dialog' to '__ch10_boss_defeat': the slot is LIVE, reached via the ch10 kill-drop path -- ch10 char_spawn_record[0] = the boss (enemy_data 54, char_id 0x7A) carries pickup_kind=2 param=0x22, so the boss's death dispatches consequence[0x22]. The page-3 dialog is his defeat/interrogation line revealing the 黃金徽章 plot. The earlier 'unref' verdict only scanned turn-event/tile-step hooks and missed the kill-drop path.
purpose: Chapter 10 boss-defeat dialog (per-event dispatch slot 0x22, reached via the ch10 kill-drop path when the boss record[0] enemy_data 54, pickup_kind=2 param=0x22, falls): shows current-chapter dialog page 3 (the boss's defeat/interrogation line, revealing the 黃金徽章 plot) and returns (shares handler_18's body).
logic_summary: Binary body is a 7-byte Class-3 shared-body consumer: PUSH 0x28; JMP 0x34901, which jumps into handler_18 @ 0x348FC at its CALL __CHK instruction (0x34901), thereby reusing handler_18's __CHK(0x28) stack probe, the 8-PUSH dialog-geometry chain at 0x34906, the JMP into the shared display tail (PUSH data_fd2_current_chapter_text; CALL fd2_display_dialog_scene; ADD ESP,0x24; RET), and the RET, all unchanged. Net effect: one call fd2_display_dialog_scene(data_fd2_current_chapter_text, page=3, 0xA0000, 0x140, 0xCD, 0x4C, 0x4A, 0x13, 1) then return. The C source reproduces this as the inline page-3 dialog call (Layer-2 equivalence; the shared-body fold is an in-binary layout artifact). No branch, no RNG, no numeric computation, return value discarded.
